digest.component_or_area: test suite — ACLI subprocess timeout and snapshot fetch stall detection sentinels
propositions: Five real-subprocess reap tests each waste ~1.01s waiting for a blanket 1s timeout deadline to expire, creating a load-dependent timing race where child setup ordering depends on interpreter startup latency rather than explicit synchronization.

The fake-child 429-retry test inherits a 1s timeout ceiling as an implicit pass condition, creating a latent load flake when the two sequential spawns must complete within that window, which shrinking a shared module-wide fixture would only worsen.

Three reap tests assert on child-side state (grandchild pidfile, spawn counter, flushed partial stdout) whose readiness is guaranteed only by the 1s window exceeding interpreter startup time, not by explicit synchronization gates.
The 2s low-speed window in the snapshot stall test exceeds the 1s window already proven sufficient by its sibling dribble test, wasting 1.06s of test runtime.

Child readiness races can be eliminated by requiring fake children to write a readiness marker as their final action before hanging, with a parent-side Popen wrapper polling for that file before returning the process, ensuring the injected timeout window is spent entirely on the hang.

PID reap assertions can be made deterministic by polling PID absence via an explicit `_wait_until_gone` helper under a hung-guard ceiling (10s–30s), rather than relying on the injected window being larger than process creation latency.
